name: KIO PUE|1 Puebla
notes: Inflect lists KIO PUE|1 at 353 Boulevard Municipio Libre, Puebla City; facility page describes it as a KIO-operated colocation data center and reports 1.8 MW. Uptime Institute also lists Puebla among KIO ATOM mobile data center deployments.

name: CloudHQ QRO Campus
notes: CloudHQ describes the QRO Campus near Querétaro airport as six buildings of 48 MW IT load each; Promexico Industry reported a USD 4.8B, 55-hectare hyperscale campus for cloud and AI services.

name: Aligned / ODATA Querétaro campus (QR01-QR04, including QR03)
notes: Aligned lists Querétaro data centers QR-01 through QR-04 and says the campus is on track for 400 MW utility capacity; ODATA announcement says DC QR03 in PyME Industrial Park will total 300 MW IT capacity and the first 72 MW building was scheduled for Q2 2025.

name: KIO Querétaro QRO1
notes: DCD reports QRO1 launched in 2007 in Parque Industrial El Marqués, with 2.5 MW and 4,100 sqm across five data halls; fifth hall launched in February 2022.

name: KIO Querétaro QRO2
notes: BNamericas reports KIO inaugurated QRO2 with 12 MW. DataCenterMap describes QRO2 in El Marqués as 12 MW IT power and 12,917 sqm at full buildout.

name: KIO third Querétaro data center (QRO3)
notes: Mexico News Daily reported KIO planned a third data center at El Marqués Industrial Park; DCD later noted KIO had announced plans for its third Querétaro data center in February 2023.

name: Ascenty México 1 and México 2 / Querétaro campus
notes: Digital Realty/Ascenty announced two Querétaro facilities, with DCD reporting initial phases in 2021 and 36 MW full buildout. Later Ascenty materials describe the Querétaro campus as part of its Mexico portfolio.

name: Equinix MX1 and MX2 Querétaro
notes: Equinix lists MX1 and MX2 as Mexico City metro data centers located in Querétaro; Dgtl Infra notes both facilities were acquired from Axtel and serve the Mexico City metro.

name: Equinix MX3 xScale Mexico City / Querétaro
notes: Dgtl Infra reported Equinix developing a Mexico City xScale facility called MX3, with first phase Mexico City 3x-1 possibly in Querétaro; exact final siting/capacity not confirmed publicly.

name: Scala San Juan del Río and Querétaro campuses
notes: Scala location page lists SMEXSJ01/03/04 and SMEXSJ02 in San Juan del Río, plus SQROQT01-04 in Querétaro, with start-up windows from 2024 to 2028; page marks some as in development and some as planned.

name: Microsoft Mexico Central cloud datacenter region
notes: Microsoft announced launch of its first hyperscale cloud datacenter region in Mexico, stating the multiple-datacenter cloud region is located in the Querétaro metropolitan area.

name: AWS Mexico Region / Querétaro cloud infrastructure
notes: El País reported AWS began a USD 5B investment in Querétaro for cloud computing, storage and AI services. Mordor states AWS activated three availability zones in Querétaro in early 2025; capacity not disclosed.

name: Google Cloud Querétaro cloud region / data center investment
notes: Guardian and Site Selection identify Google among the major cloud/data center investors driving Querétaro's data center boom; exact campus capacity and operator structure were not found in public sources.

name: Triara Querétaro Data Center
notes: Telmex/Triara official page lists Data Center TRIARA Querétaro at Epigmenio González No. 2, Col. Claustros del Parque, Querétaro.

name: Triara / Telmex Cancún Data Center
notes: DCD reported Telmex opened a Cancún data center in 2021, chosen for submarine-cable/NAP of the Americas connectivity. Telmex official Triara page lists Data Center TRIARA Cancún at Av. Yaxchilán No. 69, SM 21.

name: KIO SLP|1 San Luis Potosí
notes: Inflect lists KIO SLP|1 at 888 Vasco de Quiroga, San Luis Potosí. Uptime Institute lists San Luis Potosí among KIO ATOM mobile data center locations.

name: Flo Networks SLP/E1
notes: Inflect lists Flo Networks SLP/E1 at 270 Charro Mexicano, San Luis Potosí; Datacenters.com reports two data centers and two providers in the San Luis Potosí city market.

name: KIO HER|1 Hermosillo
notes: KIO official page lists KIO HER|1 at Calle General Bernardo Reyes No. 98, Hermosillo, Sonora, as a Tier III-level modular carrier-neutral data center for enterprise, edge and regional workloads.

name: KIO VHM|1 Villahermosa
notes: Inflect lists KIO VHM|1 in Villahermosa. Uptime Institute lists Villahermosa among KIO ATOM mobile data center deployments.

name: EdgeNet Sala Villahermosa Data Center
notes: Datacenters.com lists EdgeNet's Sala Villahermosa data center for regional colocation/connectivity. EdgeNet official site says it operates 30 AI-ready data centers in Mexico; DCD reported its 30-edge-data-center launch.

name: KIWI NETWORKS Villa Vicente Guerrero
notes: Inflect lists KIWI NETWORKS Villa Vicente Guerrero under Tabasco data centers. Source is an aggregator listing only; no independent capacity or operator details found.

name: EdgeNet Sala Reynosa Telmex Data Center
notes: Datacenters.com lists EdgeNet's Sala Reynosa Telmex facility in Reynosa, Tamaulipas; facility text reports 15.26 kW maximum power, 31 sqm core room, Telmex/Phoenix fiber, and N+1 critical systems.

name: Vertiv Reynosa Building C data-center infrastructure manufacturing expansion
notes: Not a colocation data center; included as adjacent data-center infrastructure project. Vertiv is building/expanding a 150,000-sq-ft Reynosa manufacturing facility for switchgear and power systems used in data centers and AI facilities, with reported USD 150M investment and 1,000 jobs.

name: KIO VER|1 Veracruz
notes: Inflect lists KIO VER|1 at 1325 Calle Ignacio de la Llave, Veracruz City, and reports 2 MW with N+1 power redundancy. Uptime Institute lists Veracruz among KIO ATOM mobile data center deployments.

name: KIO XAL|1 Xalapa
notes: Cloudscene lists KIO Networks XAL|1 in Xalapa with 75 sqm gross building size and 0.05 MW colocation size. Uptime Institute and Dgtl Infra list Xalapa among KIO edge/ATOM data center locations.

name: Flo Networks COR/E1 Córdoba
notes: Inflect lists Flo Networks COR/E1 at 45 Villa Verde, Córdoba, Veracruz; Datacenters.com reports three Veracruz data centers across two providers.
